Chokepoint Watch: Quantum
Monthly theme watch · quantum computing and sensing hardware · evidence, not a trade

Chokepoint Watch: Quantum

As of 2026-10-19Edition 1Previous edition: first edition
What changedThis is the first edition, so there is no baseline. Two chokepoints are on the board and both are graded lead-to-partial. Dilution-refrigerator units, TFLN foundry capacity and specialty lasers were considered and rejected.
Top chokepointqua-1, helium-3 gas for dilution refrigerators. DOE allocates "thousands of liters" a year from federal reserves, and Bluefors alone has contracted for up to 10,000 L/yr from 2028. Physical scarcity is plausible, but no primary source shows quantum demand above supply. The holder is state-run.
Next datedSilex says sample production of Q-Si (enriched silicon-28) "is expected to commence in Q1 CY2027". ASP Isotopes' FY2026 10-K (due by about 2027-03-31) should show whether its Si-28 deliveries started.

Marks: P primary, L lead, map analyst's map, not evidence. Step grades: primary lead unexamined contradicted. All quotes were captured with a fetch tool that extracts sentences rather than showing raw HTML. Quotes cut short by the tool end in "…" (see Run notes).

2Predictions settled this month

None. This is the first edition, so no earlier predictions exist.

3The board

Two chokepoints, both deep-dived. Neither reaches "supported" on demand against supply. Both are kept because a primary source states the constraint at the right layer and in a real unit.

qua-1

Helium-3 gas for dilution refrigerators

new

Layer: material (He-3 gas, ≥99.8 atom %), measured in litres per year. Downstream: the dilution refrigerator (a subsystem) used by superconducting and spin-qubit machines.

The chain

  1. National programmes fund superconducting and spin-qubit machines. About 5 of DARPA QBI's 11 Stage B firms use dilution fridges P map (the modality split is the analyst's).
  2. Each machine needs one or more dilution refrigerators P (Rigetti 10-K).
  3. Each fridge holds "a few dozen liters" of He-3 L (Interlune).
  4. US federal He-3 is allocated each year from reserves by DOE's interagency group P.
  5. The fridge maker contracts for a large forward supply: Bluefors, up to 10,000 L/yr from 2028 P.
Constraint primary

Litres of He-3 per year. US federal supply is "thousands of liters". Allocation is administered, not auctioned.

"Each year, thousands of liters of He-3 gas are made available"DOE Isotope Program (NIDC) · Supply and Demand of Helium-3 · undated page, read 2026-10-19 · isotopes.gov
"The IRP leads the Interagency Group on He-3 to determine annual federal allocations from reserves."DOE · FY2026 Congressional Justification, Isotope R&D and Production, p.254 · 2025-07 · energy.gov PDF (repeated in the FY2027 request, p.258)
Demand vs supply lead

The evidence here is one supply contract, not an order backlog. Bluefors' ceiling of 10,000 L/yr is about the size of the entire US federal supply (an estimate; CRS put new US supply near 8,000 L/yr in 2011). That shows intent to source at scale. It does not prove that today's demand exceeds supply. Every explicit "demand exceeds supply" statement found comes from a would-be supplier (Interlune, Black Moon, Pulsar Helium), so those are leads.

"Bluefors has agreed to purchase up to ten thousand liters of helium-3 annually, for delivery from 2028 to 2037."Bluefors (counterparty) · press release on the Interlune agreement · 2025-09-16 · bluefors.com
"In the coming years, the demand for helium-3 will rise sharply to power this next phase of quantum industry growth."Bluefors · same release (forecast, not orders)
"projected Federal demand for He-3 is now less than 6,000 liters per year."DOE Isotope Program · Supply and Demand of Helium-3 · isotopes.gov (federal demand only, not commercial or quantum demand)
"Helium-3 remains exceptionally scarce, expensive and tightly regulated."Pulsar Helium (would-be supplier) · 2026-07-10 · release PDF · L, self-interested
Relief lead

Lunar He-3 deliveries are contracted for 2028–2037 (Bluefors) and 2029–2035 (Maybell, per Interlune), and no supplier has delivered yet. DOE's own purchase of 3 litres from Interlune is due "no later than April 2029" (Interlune's release only; no DOE confirmation was found). DOE's FY2027 request describes "growth in heavy water and helium-3 inventory…" (excerpt). Terrestrial relief from Canadian supply appears only in 2011 CRS material. Relief horizon: 2028 at the earliest, and unproven.

Control primary

In the US, the DOE Isotope Program is the sole federal seller. Russian exports, once about 25,000 L/yr, were suspended (CRS 2011). Shares today are not published.

"the He-3 supply was impacted by an unexpected reduction of Russian exports to the marketplace."DOE Isotope Program · Supply and Demand of Helium-3 · isotopes.gov
Capture lead

A state books the economics. DOE prices sales to commercial customers at "full-cost recovery or market price…" (FY2026 request, p.252, excerpt). No current price per litre was found. CRS (2011) reported auction prices of $40–85/L before 2009 and commercial prices of "$2,000 per liter or more" after the shortage was found. Cost share, estimate: a few dozen litres at about $2,000/L is roughly $50–70k per fridge. Against a dilution refrigerator priced in the high hundreds of thousands of dollars (map, unsourced), that is roughly 5–15% of the subsystem.

Invalidation lead

Several observations argue against a binding shortage:

  • DOE's 2026 documents describe He-3 inventory growing and frame it as stewardship, not crisis.
  • The DOE World Quantum Day page (2026-04-14) names quantum as a "critical role" for He-3 but gives no shortfall.
  • Bluefors' revenue was roughly flat from 2023 to 2025 (L, registry data). That does not suggest fridge output is being rationed by gas supply.
  • About half the QBI Stage B field (neutral atom, trapped ion, photonic) needs no dilution fridge.

Physical scarcity

Plausible, lead-grade. The constraint and its unit are primary. A shortfall against quantum demand is not shown.

Economic capture

State. DOE prices at full cost or market. No current price is published, so pricing power is unproven.

Investability

Not investable through the holder. The holder is the US DOE, a state body (Russia's position is unexamined). Would-be suppliers Interlune and Black Moon are private and pre-revenue for He-3.

Bear checks

CheckFinding
DilutionNot applicable to the state holder. The private would-be suppliers are venture-funded.
GAAP marginsNot applicable. DOE prices at full-cost recovery or market price.
Customer concentrationUnexamined. Federal users (neutron detection, research) compete with commercial quantum buyers for the same allocation.
Cash vs debtNot applicable.
Second source qualifyingLunar suppliers are contracted but not delivering before 2028. Canadian supply is unexamined after 2011.
Design bypassReal. Neutral-atom, trapped-ion and photonic machines need no dilution fridge (DARPA QBI Stage B list, P; IonQ 10-K, P).
Roadmap slipsA slip would reduce demand and relieve the constraint.
Programme cutsNot checked this month.
Layer errorThe risk is real. "Quantum needs He-3" claims often blur the gas (material) and the fridge (subsystem). This card claims only the gas layer, and the fridge layer is rejected separately.

Kill criteria

  • DOE publishes an allocation or sales notice showing commercial He-3 requests met in full for two consecutive years.
  • A fridge maker (Bluefors, Maybell, Quantum Design) or a DOE document states that He-3 availability is not limiting fridge deliveries.
  • DOE or another government source reports a non-US, non-Russian supply (for example Canadian) entering the market at more than 1,000 L/yr before 2028.
qua-p1 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-04-19 · openBy 2027-04-19, no DOE Isotope Program document (isotopes.gov page, notice or budget justification) will state that helium-3 demand exceeds available federal supply. DOE will continue to describe He-3 as allocated annually from reserves by the interagency group. Shown by DOE Isotope Program web pages and budget documents.

Consensus check: the earliest primary evidence found is CRS R41419 (2011-10-06) on the He-3 shortage. The quantum-specific angle dates from 2025 (Bluefors, 2025-09-16). The scarcity theme is consensus; the size of the quantum demand is still unproven.

qua-2

Isotopically enriched silicon-28 for spin qubits

new

Layer: material (enriched Si-28 feedstock), measured in kilograms per year. Downstream: spin-qubit wafers and chips. This card covers supply, volumes and contracts only; how the isotope is produced is out of scope.

The chain

  1. Spin-qubit programmes are running. Diraq, Quantum Motion and Silicon Quantum Computing are in DARPA QBI Stage B P.
  2. Spin qubits need Si-28-enriched silicon map.
  3. The market is under 50 kg/yr and was historically sourced from Russia P (Silex).
  4. Non-Russian supply is pre-volume. Silex samples are due in Q1 CY2027 P. ASP Isotopes' Si-28 deliveries were due in Q1 2026 P, and a press report puts them in Q3 L.
Constraint primary

Kilograms of qualified, non-Russian Si-28 per year. Supply today is near zero and the first module is sized at 20 kg/yr.

"Historically, enriched silicon was primarily sourced from Russia"Silex Systems · ASX announcement, Silex Quantum Silicon Production Plant Update – Construction Completed, Commissioning Underway · 2026-06-29 · ASX PDF
"The initial Q-Si production module will produce up to 20kg of Q-Si annually"Silex Systems · same announcement
Demand vs supply lead

Demand is stated by the would-be holder's own market analysis (a forecast, not orders). One offtake partner and one unnamed US contract exist, neither with a volume. This is a timing and qualification gap, not a proven volume shortfall.

"Internal market analysis indicates the current market is small (less than 50 kgs per year)"Silex Systems · same announcement
"Silex is currently working with its first commercial offtake partner, Silicon Quantum Computing Pty Ltd,"Silex Systems · same announcement (offtake partner, volume not disclosed)
"This represents the Company's largest silicon-28 contract to date."ASP Isotopes · press release EX-99.1, Business Updates · 2025-10-13 · sec.gov (US customer unnamed; deliveries "expected during Q1 2026")
Relief primary
"Sample production of highly enriched silicon-28 is expected to commence in Q1 CY2027."Silex Systems · ASX announcement · 2026-06-29

A 20 kg/yr module set against a market of under 50 kg/yr implies relief within about 12–24 months of qualification, if the samples qualify. ASP Isotopes' delivery date may have slipped from Q1 to Q3 2026 (Creamer Media, 2026-05-26, snippet only, L).

Control primary

Historically Russia (Silex's words; share not quantified). Emerging holders are Silex (ASX) and ASP Isotopes (Nasdaq; plant in South Africa). Urenco and others were not evidenced this run.

Capture unexamined

No price or pricing-power statement was found. The total market is under 50 kg/yr, so the absolute economics are small for any holder. Cost share, estimate: negligible per spin-qubit chip (grams per wafer), but gating for qualification.

Invalidation lead

The volumes are tiny. A single 20 kg module could cover a large share of the stated market. The dilution-fridge-using spin-qubit firms are a minority of QBI Stage B. Spin-qubit groups also hold earlier Si-28 stock (unexamined).

Physical scarcity

Near-term only (12–24 months), lead-grade. Non-Russian qualified supply is pre-volume; the long-run gap is small.

Economic capture

Unproven. The market is under 50 kg/yr and no price was found.

Investability

Weak. Silex is listed, but Q-Si is a small part of a group centred on uranium enrichment (GLE). ASP Isotopes is listed; its dilution and margins were not examined this run.

Bear checks

CheckFinding
DilutionUnexamined for ASP Isotopes and for Silex.
GAAP marginsUnexamined. Q-Si is not yet producing.
Customer concentrationHigh. Silex names one offtake partner (SQC), and ASP Isotopes names one US customer, unnamed.
Cash vs debtUnexamined.
Second source qualifyingTwo non-Russian entrants are in progress, which argues for relief.
Design bypassOther modalities need no Si-28. Some spin-qubit work uses natural silicon or germanium (map).
Roadmap slipsA slip lowers demand, and ASP Isotopes' delivery may have slipped too (L).
Programme cutsNot checked.
Layer errorThe card holds to the material layer. No claim is made about qubit chips.

Kill criteria

  • Silex reports Q-Si samples delivered and qualified by SQC (expected 2027).
  • ASP Isotopes reports Si-28 deliveries to its US customer in a 10-Q or 10-K.
  • A spin-qubit maker (Diraq, Quantum Motion, SQC, Intel) states it has adequate Si-28 supply from a non-Russian source.
qua-p2 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-04-30 · openBy 2027-04-30, Silex will report in an ASX announcement or its quarterly activities report that sample production of highly enriched silicon-28 (Q-Si) has commenced. Shown by Silex Systems ASX announcements.
qua-p3 · made 2026-10-19 · deadline 2027-04-15 · openBy 2027-04-15, ASP Isotopes' annual report on Form 10-K for FY2026 will state that silicon-28 deliveries to its US customer have begun. Shown by ASP Isotopes' SEC filing.

Consensus check: the earliest primary evidence found is ASP Isotopes' release of 2025-10-13; the Silex detail dates from 2026-06-29. The theme is early, barely reported outside specialist press.

5Cross-theme hooks

  • Helium-3 is also allocated to neutron detectors for defence, security and border screening. Federal and quantum users draw on the same DOE allocation (Aerospace and Defence theme).
  • TFLN and silicon-photonics foundries (UMC/HyperLight, GlobalFoundries) are shared with datacom optics, where AI demand sets the capacity (Photonics theme).
  • Stable-isotope enrichment capacity overlaps with nuclear fuel. Silex's Q-Si sits inside a group whose main business is uranium enrichment (a possible nuclear theme).

6Council questions

The latest Chokepoint Council (edition 1, 2026-10-19) assigns no questions to the quantum theme. Quantum is not on its theme roll. There is nothing to answer this month.

7Next questions

  1. What is DOE's annual He-3 allocation volume and its current price per litre? Look at isotopes.gov product and ordering pages, the full FY2027 IRP justification text, and any Federal Register notice.
  2. Do Maybell or Quantum Design confirm He-3 contracts or state that He-3 limits deliveries? Look at company releases and Bluefors' 2025 financial statements in the Finnish registry.
  3. What is the status of Silex's Q-Si commissioning? Look at Silex's September-quarter activities report (late October 2026) and its AGM materials.
  4. Have ASP Isotopes' Si-28 deliveries started? Look at its Q3 2026 10-Q (about mid-November).
  5. Do the filings of IBM, D-Wave and Rigetti (full risk factors) or the S-1s of Quantinuum and Infleqtion name a sole-source fridge, gas or laser supplier? Look at SEC EDGAR full text.

8Run notes

  • Edition: no artifact titled "Chokepoint Watch: Quantum" existed among the user's 69 artifacts, so this is edition 1 and a new artifact. No earlier contents were assumed.
  • Quote fidelity: every quote was captured by WebFetch, which runs pages through an extraction model and does not show raw HTML. Sub-agents report the quoted sentences as extracted verbatim. Several were truncated at about 125 characters and are marked "…" or described as excerpts. P items rest on these extractions, so treat them as near-verbatim.
  • Downgraded to lead: all Interlune claims, including DOE's purchase of 3 L by April 2029 and the Maybell offtake, because no DOE or Maybell confirmation was found. Also downgraded: the Black Moon DOE contract (wire release), Pulsar Helium, Bluefors registry revenue (via Asiakastieto, not a filing), Bluefors' 2024 "stories" page, the Creamer Media report on ASP Isotopes' delivery slip (snippet only), and the Vexlum funding (snippet only).
  • Unreachable or incomplete: CRS R48144 (blocked by robots.txt); the full QCi 10-Q (only a mirror was available); the Rigetti 10-K (about 113k characters read, risk factors possibly incomplete); the Infleqtion S-1 beyond 100k characters; CRS R41419 (first 100k of about 108k characters).
  • Not checked: ULVAC, Leiden Cryogenics, ICEoxford, Zero Point Cryogenics, Low Noise Factory, the FormFactor 10-K, IBM and D-Wave filings, Toptica, NKT/Hamamatsu, SNSPD makers, and European and Japanese national programme budgets. These are gaps, not negatives.
  • Out of scope, respected: no research on isotope production methods or on weapons. No share prices were used.
  • Tool calls: about 84. That is 7 in the main session (two artifact listings, one council read, one skill load, the write, the publish, one notification) and 77 across three research sub-agents (24, 27 and 26). This is slightly over the budget of about 80.
